verses.text: How terrible for the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim, and for the fading flower of its glorious beauty, set on the head of the fertile valley, the city of those overcome by wine!
Look, the Lord has someone who is mighty and strong. Like a hailstorm, a destroying storm, like a flood of powerful overflowing waters, he will throw that crown down to the ground with his hand.
The proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim will be trampled underfoot.
The fading flower of its glorious beauty, set on the head of the fertile valley, will be like a fig that ripens before the summer harvest. As soon as someone sees it, they pick it and eat it.
On that day the LORD of Armies will be a glorious crown and a beautiful wreath for those of his people who are left.
He will give a spirit of justice to the one who sits as judge, and strength to those who turn back the enemy at the gate.

But these also stagger from wine and stumble from strong drink. Priests and prophets stagger from strong drink. They are confused by wine. They stumble from strong drink. They make mistakes when they see visions. They stumble when they make decisions.
All their tables are covered with vomit and filth. There is no clean place left.
They say, "Who does he think he is teaching? Who is he explaining his message to? Babies who have just stopped drinking milk, who have just been taken from the breast?
For he says: rule on rule, rule on rule, line on line, line on line, a little here, a little there."
So God will speak to this people through strange lips and a foreign language.
He told them, "This is the place of rest. Let the tired rest. This is the place of peace." But they would not listen.

So the word of the LORD to them will become: rule on rule, rule on rule, line on line, line on line, a little here, a little there. Then they will go, fall backward, and be broken. They will be trapped and captured.
So listen to the word of the LORD, you mockers who rule these people in Jerusalem.

You say, "We have made a covenant with death. We have made a deal with the grave. When the overwhelming flood sweeps by, it cannot touch us, for we have made lies our hiding place, and we have hidden ourselves behind falsehood."
So this is what the Lord GOD says: "Look, I am laying a stone in Zion as a foundation, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone for a firm foundation. Whoever believes will never panic.
I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the level. Hail will sweep away your hiding place of lies, and water will flood your hiding place.
Your covenant with death will be canceled. Your deal with the grave will not stand. When the overwhelming flood sweeps by, you will be beaten down by it.
Every time it comes, it will carry you away. It will come morning after morning, by day and by night. Understanding this message will bring nothing but terror."
The bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket is too narrow to wrap yourself in.
For the LORD will rise up as he did at Mount Perazim. He will be angry as he was in the Valley of Gibeon. He will do his work, his strange work, and carry out his task, his unusual task.
So now, stop mocking, or your chains will become heavier. For I have heard from the Lord GOD of Armies that destruction has been decided against the whole land.
Listen and hear my voice! Pay attention and hear what I say!
Does a farmer keep plowing all the time to plant? Does he keep breaking up and turning over the soil?
When he has made the ground level, does he not scatter dill and sow cumin? Does he not plant wheat in rows, barley in its proper place, and spelt along the edges?
His God teaches him and shows him the right way.
Dill is not threshed with a heavy sledge, and a cart wheel is not rolled over cumin. Instead, dill is beaten out with a stick, and cumin with a rod.
Grain for bread must be crushed, but he does not keep threshing it forever. He drives the wheels of his cart over it, but his horses do not crush it to powder.
This also comes from the LORD of Armies, whose plans are wonderful and whose wisdom is great.
